Inflation is America’s biggest concern:

In November, a record 57% of US consumers cited higher prices as a reason for their financial situation worsening compared with a year earlier.

This figure has surged +24 percentage points since March 2024.

By comparison, this proportion peaked at 48% during the 2008 Financial Crisis and the Great Inflation of the 1970s.

To put this into perspective, in April 2020, just 2% of consumers cited higher prices as a reason for their financial situation worsening compared with a year earlier.

Meanwhile, 40% of US consumers expect their financial situation to deteriorate over the next 12 months, the 2nd-highest reading on record.

Inflation remains far too high in the US.

Market corrections are a regular phenomenon:

The US equity market has recorded an average of 1 correction of 10%+ per year since 1930.

Since 2000, the S&P 500 has seen 24 regular corrections.

Despite these declines, the S&P 500 has delivered positive annual returns in 19 calendar years since 2000.

Furthermore, US stocks have posted 3.4 pullbacks of 5%+ per year on average since 1930.

By comparison, a bear market has occurred once every 3.3 years on average over the same period.

Market corrections are a natural feature of equity markets.

Traditional and onchain finance continue to converge.

As tokenization has become increasingly popular in US markets, tokenized stock on Solana can now serve as collateral.

For example, owners of Ondo's tokenized Tesla stock, $TSLA, can be utilized as collateral for DeFi lending.

This means investors can now obtain liquidity without directly selling exposure to the underlying asset.

Meanwhile, institutional activity now includes JP Morgan, BNY Mellon, State Street, and others using Solana-related infrastructure in different capacities.

This shift has driven tokenized equity supply on Solana to over $600 million, up +210% YTD despite the broader market drawdown.

Jupiter, the largest onchain platform on Solana, has reported a 72% QoQ increase in volume in these tokenized assets amid the shift.

The future of finance is quickly moving toward tokenization and more efficient transactions.

The S&P 500 outperformed the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index by +2.1 percentage points on Monday, its largest daily outperformance since at least 1990.

At the close, the S&P 500 was up +4.7%, while the Equal-Weight Index gained +2.6%.

The divergence comes as the S&P 500 Information Technology sector led the market, surging +9.0%, its strongest daily performance since April 9th, 2025.

Nvidia, $NVDA, alone accounted for 34% of the S&P 500's return on Monday.
